nvitk.db
========

.. py:module:: nvitk.db

.. autoapi-nested-parse::

   Dataset catalog, SQLite index, XNAT helpers, imports, and :class:`~nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo`.

   Configure the tree with ``NVITK_DATASET_ROOT`` or pass ``root=`` to ``DataRepo``.

.. py:class:: DatasetCatalog(root: str | pathlib.Path)

   Load and update ``catalog/repository.json``, resolve table paths, variables, and pipelines.

   Use :meth:`get_table` for :class:`TableDefinition` rows and :meth:`list_tables` for names.


   .. py:attribute:: REQUIRED_REPOSITORY_KEYS


   .. py:attribute:: REQUIRED_TABLE_KEYS


   .. py:attribute:: REQUIRED_VARIABLE_KEYS


   .. py:attribute:: root


   .. py:attribute:: repository_path


   .. py:attribute:: repository_manifest
      :type:  dict[str, Any]


   .. py:attribute:: tables_manifest
      :type:  dict[str, Any]


   .. py:attribute:: variables_manifest
      :type:  dict[str, Any]


   .. py:attribute:: pipelines_manifest
      :type:  dict[str, Any]


   .. py:attribute:: pipelines_manifest_path
      :type:  pathlib.Path | None
      :value: None



   .. py:attribute:: _tables
      :type:  dict[str, TableDefinition]


   .. py:method:: create_scaffold(root: str | pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path
      :classmethod:


      Create a minimal dataset tree at *root* by copying the packaged catalog templates
      (manifests + schema) and creating empty ``tables/``/``cache/`` directories.



   .. py:method:: refresh() -> None

      Re-read all manifest JSON files from disk and rebuild the in-memory :class:`TableDefinition`
      cache. Called after every catalog mutation to keep this instance consistent with disk.



   .. py:property:: sqlite_index_path
      :type: pathlib.Path


      Absolute path to the SQLite query-cache database declared in the repository manifest.


   .. py:property:: table_root
      :type: pathlib.Path


      Absolute path to the directory holding this dataset's Parquet table files.


   .. py:method:: list_tables() -> list[str]

      Sorted names of every table registered in the manifest.



   .. py:method:: get_table(name: str) -> TableDefinition

      Return *name*'s :class:`TableDefinition`, raising ``TableNotFoundError`` if unregistered.



   .. py:method:: table_exists(name: str) -> bool

      True if *name* is a registered table.



   .. py:method:: ensure_table_definition(name: str, *, clone_from: str) -> pathlib.Path

      Register *name* in ``tables.json`` by cloning manifest metadata from *clone_from*,
      pointing at ``<table_root>/{name}.parquet``. Creates an empty Parquet file if missing.

      No-op (returns existing Parquet path) when *name* is already registered.



   .. py:method:: ensure_cognitive_measurements_table() -> pathlib.Path

      Register ``cognitive_measurements`` with the canonical long-form schema.



   .. py:method:: list_pipelines(modality: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

      All pipeline entries, or just those matching *modality* (case-insensitive) if given.



   .. py:method:: default_pipeline_id(modality: str) -> str | None

      The ``pipeline_id`` flagged ``is_default`` for *modality*, or ``None`` if none is set.



   .. py:method:: pipeline_ids_for_role(role: str) -> list[str]

      ``pipeline_id`` values for every pipeline entry tagged with *role*.



   .. py:method:: all_pipeline_ids() -> set[str]

      Set of every registered ``pipeline_id`` across all modalities.



   .. py:method:: _pipeline_entries_for_modality(modality: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

      Pipeline entries for *modality* (case-insensitive), or all entries if *modality* is unset.



   .. py:method:: _normalize_pipeline_tokens(selector: str | int | Iterable[str | int] | None) -> list[str]
      :staticmethod:


      Coerce a pipeline *selector* (a single str/int or an iterable of them) into a flat list of
      non-empty stripped string tokens.



   .. py:method:: resolve_pipeline_selector(selector: str | int | Iterable[str | int] | None, *, modality: str | None = None) -> list[str] | None

      Return None to apply catalog defaults per modality in ``DataRepo.image``.
      Otherwise return an explicit ``pipeline_id`` list.

      Aliases from ``measurement_pipelines.json`` (including integers like ``1`` / ``2``) resolve
      within the pipelines for ``modality`` when provided; without ``modality``, ambiguous aliases
      raise ``ManifestError``.



   .. py:method:: validate_pipelines_manifest(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None

      Validate the pipelines manifest structure and reject duplicate ``is_default`` pipelines within
      the same modality; raises ``ManifestError`` on any violation.



   .. py:method:: variable_entries(*, domain: str | None = None, table: str | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

      Registered variable entries, optionally filtered by ``domain`` and/or ``table``.



   .. py:method:: resolve_variable_ids(requested: str | Iterable[str] | None, *, domain: str | None = None) -> list[str]

      Resolve *requested* names/aliases/source-column names/labels to canonical ``variable_id``
      values (case- and normalization-insensitive), leaving any unmatched entries unchanged.



   .. py:method:: register_variables(entries: list[dict[str, Any]], *, merge: bool = True) -> None

      Add or update *entries* in the variables manifest (merging into existing entries with the same
      ``variable_id`` when ``merge`` is True, otherwise overwriting), then persist and reload.



   .. py:method:: _merge_variable_entry(existing: dict[str, Any], new: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]

      Merge *new* onto *existing*: union+de-dupe ``aliases``, and for every other key skip empty
      strings/lists/None in *new* so a partial update never blanks out existing metadata.



   .. py:method:: update_table_schema(name: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, *, provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, path: str | None = None) -> None

      Update (or create) *name*'s entry in the tables manifest from *df*'s inferred dtypes, row
      count, and optional *provenance*/``path``, then persist and reload.



   .. py:method:: clear_table(name: str) -> None

      Delete the Parquet file for ``name`` if present and set ``row_count`` to 0 in the manifest.



   .. py:method:: validate_repository_manifest(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None

      Raise ``ManifestError`` if *payload* is missing any ``REQUIRED_REPOSITORY_KEYS``.



   .. py:method:: validate_tables_manifest(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None

      Raise ``ManifestError`` if *payload*'s ``tables`` object or any entry is malformed.



   .. py:method:: validate_variables_manifest(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None

      Raise ``ManifestError`` if *payload* lacks a ``variables`` list, or if any entry is invalid.



   .. py:method:: _validate_variable_entry(entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None

      Raise ``ManifestError``/``ValidationError`` if *entry* is missing required keys or has a
      blank ``variable_id``.

.. py:function:: build_clinical_measurement_rows(agg: pandas.DataFrame, spec: DerivedClinicalMeasurementSpec) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Map an aggregate frame to ``clinical_measurements`` columns (one derived variable).

   As with the image builder, a categorical / text ``spec.value_kind`` routes the value to
   ``value_text`` rather than ``value_num``.


.. py:function:: build_image_measurement_rows(agg: pandas.DataFrame, spec: DerivedImageMeasurementSpec) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Map an aggregate frame to ``image_measurements`` columns (one derived variable).

   ``agg`` must include ``subject_uid`` and the column named by ``spec.value_column``.
   Optional columns copied through when present: ``session_id``, ``region_id``,
   ``region_label``, ``frame_index``. A categorical / text ``spec.value_kind`` routes the value to
   ``value_text`` instead of ``value_num`` (see :func:`_split_values`).


.. py:function:: publish_derived_measurements(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, df: pandas.DataFrame, *, table: Literal['image_measurements', 'clinical_measurements', 'cognitive_measurements'], register: DerivedVariableRegistration | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, build_sqlite_index: bool = True, upsert_key_columns: list[str] | None = None, allow_empty: bool = False) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Upsert derived measurement rows and optionally register catalog metadata.

   Pass the dataframe returned by :func:`build_image_measurement_rows` or
   :func:`build_clinical_measurement_rows` (the latter also matches the
   ``cognitive_measurements`` schema). When ``register`` is set, that entry
   is written with :func:`register_derived_variable` after a successful upsert.


.. py:function:: register_derived_variable(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, entry: DerivedVariableRegistration | Mapping[str, Any]) -> None

   Register one variable in the dataset catalog (merge semantics by default).


.. py:function:: import_measurements_from_source(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, source_path: str | pathlib.Path, *, kind: str, source_batch_id: str, modality: str | None = None, sheet_name: str | int = 0) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Load a tabular source and import it as clinical or image measurements, per *kind*.


.. py:function:: import_pesabrain_curated_tables(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, db_base_path: str | pathlib.Path, *, source_batch_id: str | None = None, build_sqlite_index: bool = False, cohort_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]

   Alias for :func:`import_pesabrain_db_directory` kept for call sites that import the "curated"
   (already-cleaned) PESA-Brain table set; the underlying directory-scan logic is identical.


.. py:function:: import_pesabrain_source(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, db_base_path: str | pathlib.Path, filename: str, *, sheet: str | None = None, source_kind: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None, rebuild_subjects: bool = True, build_sqlite_index: bool = False, pipeline_id: str | None = None, cohort_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]

   Import a single named file from ``db_base_path``, resolving it against the configured PESA-Brain
   source specs (optionally narrowed by ``sheet``/``source_kind`` when a filename maps to more than one
   spec). Enrolls any resulting subjects into ``cohort_id`` and, unless ``rebuild_subjects`` is False,
   refreshes the ``subjects`` table. Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` if the directory or file is missing, and
   ``ValueError`` if the filename matches zero or multiple specs.


.. py:function:: import_subject_ids_from_source(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, source_path: str | pathlib.Path, *, source_batch_id: str, id_source: str | None = None, sheet_name: str = 'Sheet1') -> pandas.DataFrame

   Load a tabular source and harvest its identifier columns into ``subject_ids``.


.. py:function:: list_pesabrain_sources() -> list[dict[str, Any]]

   Flatten the ``PESABRAIN_DB_SPECS`` registry into a list of source-metadata dicts, for listing/CLI display.


.. py:function:: upsert_cohort_membership_for_subjects(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, cohort_id: str, subject_uids: Iterable[str], *, source_batch_id: str, membership_source: str = 'import') -> pandas.DataFrame

   Register ``subject_uid`` values as members of ``cohort_id`` (upserts ``cohort_membership``).


.. py:data:: ASL_ATLAS_REGIONS
   :type:  dict[str, tuple[str, Ellipsis]]

.. py:function:: regions_for_atlas(name: str) -> list[str]

   Return normalized ``region_id`` values for a named ASL atlas preset.


.. py:function:: register_t1_atlas_regions(atlas: str, region_ids: Iterable[str]) -> None

   Merge normalized region tokens into the named T1 atlas (cortical / subcortical).


.. py:function:: regions_for_t1_atlas(name: str) -> list[str]

   Return normalized ``region_id`` values for a named T1 atlas preset.


.. py:data:: DEFAULT_COHORT_ID
   :value: 'PESA-Brain'


.. py:class:: DataRepo(root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, *, use_sqlite: bool = True, auto_scaffold: bool = False)

   Dataset-facing API: load tables, clinical/image measurements, assets, scans, and writes.

   Queries prefer the SQLite index when ``use_sqlite`` is True and the index file exists;
   otherwise fall back to Parquet. Cohort filtering uses ``cohort_membership`` when present
   unless ``cohort_id=False`` (disable) or an explicit cohort id is passed.


   .. py:attribute:: root


   .. py:attribute:: catalog


   .. py:attribute:: sqlite


   .. py:attribute:: use_sqlite
      :value: True



   .. py:method:: list_tables() -> list[str]

      Registered table names from the catalog manifest.



   .. py:method:: _resolve_cohort(cohort_id: str | bool | None, filters: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> tuple[str | bool, dict[str, Any]]

      Return ``(effective_cohort, filters_without_cohort_id)``. ``False`` = do not filter by cohort.



   .. py:method:: _cohort_subject_uid_set(cohort_id: str) -> set[str] | None

      Subjects in ``cohort_membership`` for ``cohort_id``; ``None`` if table missing or empty (no filtering).



   .. py:method:: _filter_dataframe_by_cohort(df: pandas.DataFrame, cohort_id: str) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Restrict *df* to rows whose ``subject_uid`` belongs to *cohort_id*; no-op if cohort membership
      is unavailable or *df* has no ``subject_uid`` column.



   .. py:method:: _measurement_column_names(table_name: str) -> set[str]

      Column names declared in the catalog manifest for *table_name*.



   .. py:method:: _split_measurement_filters(filters: dict[str, Any] | None, *, domain: str, table_name: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[tuple[str, Any]], dict[str, str]]

      Split a user-supplied ``filters`` dict into structural column filters (applied directly to the
      measurement table) and per-variable value filters (applied against ``value_num``/``value_text``
      rows for a specific ``variable_id``), resolving any variable aliases along the way. Returns
      ``(structural_filters, [(variable_id, spec), ...], canonical_to_alias)``.



   .. py:method:: _rename_measurement_wide_columns(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, table_name: str, canonical_to_alias: dict[str, str]) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Rename wide-pivot columns from canonical variable ids back to the aliases the caller requested
      (image-measurement columns via suffix rewriting, other tables via a direct column rename).



   .. py:method:: _load_table_frame(table: str, *, columns: list[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, force_parquet: bool = False) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Load *table* via SQLite (if enabled/available) with a Parquet fallback on query failure,
      coercing the result to the manifest's declared column dtypes.



   .. py:method:: get(table: str, *, columns: list[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, wide: bool = False, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Load *table* as a DataFrame with optional column projection, filters, and wide pivot.

      For ``clinical_measurements`` / ``image_measurements`` / ``cognitive_measurements``,
      ``wide=True`` resolves values and pivots to one column per variable (and entity keys);
      see catalog wide definitions.



   .. py:method:: cognitive(*, variables: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, wide: bool = True, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Query ``cognitive_measurements`` like :meth:`clinical` but with ``domain='cognitive'``.



   .. py:method:: clinical(*, variables: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, wide: bool = True, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Query ``clinical_measurements`` with variable resolution, optional value filters, and cohort scope.

      Non-reserved *filters* keys are treated as variable ids with comparison specs (see
      :func:`~nvitk.db.filters.apply_filters`). Set ``wide=False`` for long (tidy) form.



   .. py:method:: image(*, modality: str | None = None, variables: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, regions: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, atlas: str | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, wide: bool = True, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, pipeline: str | int | Iterable[str | int] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Query ``image_measurements`` with modality, regions, atlas (ASL or T1), pipeline selection, and filters.

      When neither modality nor pipeline filters are given, rows are restricted to catalog
      default pipelines per modality where defined. Use ``atlas=`` with ``modality='asl'`` or
      ``modality='t1'`` to expand *regions* from a named atlas preset.



   .. py:method:: _filter_image_rows_to_catalog_defaults(df: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Keep rows where each modality with a catalog default matches that pipeline_id; other modalities pass through.



   .. py:method:: _assets_to_wide(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, value_column: str = 'asset_path') -> pandas.DataFrame

      One row per ``subject_uid``; column names are ``asset_slot`` values (paths in cells by default).



   .. py:method:: assets(*, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, modality: str | None = None, asset_type: str | None = None, resource_label: str | None = None, subject_uid: str | None = None, session_uid: str | None = None, pipeline_id: str | None = None, asset_slot: str | None = None, source: str | None = None, wide: bool = False, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, value: str = 'asset_path', get_image: bool = False, imread_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame | Any

      Query the ``assets`` table; optionally pivot to one row per ``subject_uid`` (``wide=True``).

      With ``get_image=True``, resolve paths to :func:`nvitk.io.imageio.imread` jobs (NIfTI
      directories expand to multiple volumes; JSON sidecars are picked up when present).
      ``imread_kwargs`` is forwarded to ``imread``; ``value`` selects the path column to read.



   .. py:method:: asset(*, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, modality: str | None = None, asset_type: str | None = None, resource_label: str | None = None, subject_uid: str | None = None, session_uid: str | None = None, pipeline_id: str | None = None, asset_slot: str | None = None, source: str | None = None, wide: bool = True, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, value: str = 'asset_path', get_image: bool = False, imread_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame | Any

      Assets as a wide table (one row per subject) by default; see :meth:`assets`.



   .. py:method:: scans(*, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None, scan_uid: str | None = None, session_uid: str | None = None, subject_uid: str | None = None, scan_id: str | None = None, modality: str | None = None, orientation: str | None = None, resource_label: str | None = None, asset_slot: str | None = None, quality: str | None = None, series_description: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None, use_sqlite: bool | None = True, path_column: str = 'local_cache_path', get_image: bool = False, asset_type: str | None = None, download_scan_path: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, xnat_config: nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig | None = None, skip_existing_download: bool = True, imread_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None, cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame | Any

      Query the ``scans`` table; with ``get_image=True``, load volumes from ``path_column``.

      Missing local paths can trigger XNAT download when ``xnat_config`` or env/profile resolves;
      use ``download_scan_path`` for a persistent cache directory. ``asset_type`` must be
      ``dicom`` or ``nifti`` for on-demand download; ``imread_kwargs`` passes through to ``imread``.



   .. py:method:: join(frames: Iterable[pandas.DataFrame], *, on: str | list[str] = 'subject_uid', how: str = 'left', cohort_id: str | bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Merge multiple DataFrames on *on* (default ``subject_uid``); optionally filter by cohort after join.



   .. py:method:: _enforce_measurement_columns(table: str, df: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Restrict *df* to the columns allowed for a known measurement *table*; pass through unchanged
      for tables not listed in ``MEASUREMENT_TABLE_COLUMNS``.



   .. py:method:: write_table(table: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, *, provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, build_sqlite_index: bool = False) -> pathlib.Path

      Write *df* to the table's Parquet file and refresh catalog schema metadata.

      Set ``build_sqlite_index=True`` to rebuild the SQLite index for *table* after the write.



   .. py:method:: upsert_table(table: str, df: pandas.DataFrame, *, key_columns: list[str] | None = None, provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, build_sqlite_index: bool = False) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Append *df* to the existing table and drop duplicates on *key_columns* (default: manifest keys).

      Always reads the current Parquet (not SQLite) so sequential upserts without an
      intervening index rebuild do not drop recently written rows.

      Returns the combined frame after :meth:`write_table`.



   .. py:method:: build_sqlite_index(*, tables: list[str] | None = None) -> pathlib.Path

      Rebuild the SQLite index from Parquet (all tables or the subset *tables*).



   .. py:method:: register_variables(entries: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None

      Register variable definitions in the catalog manifest (clinical/image domains).



   .. py:method:: drop_table(name: str, *, remove_sqlite: bool = True) -> None

      Clear *name* from the catalog; optionally delete the SQLite DB file if ``remove_sqlite``.



   .. py:method:: drop_all_tables(*, remove_sqlite: bool = True) -> None

      Clear every registered table; optionally remove the SQLite index file once at the end.



   .. py:method:: _read_table(definition: nvitk.db.catalog.TableDefinition, *, columns: list[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Read *definition*'s Parquet file (an empty typed frame if it doesn't exist yet), coerce to the
      manifest schema, and apply *filters*.



   .. py:method:: _prepare_measurements(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, wide: bool, table_name: str, image_wide_single_variable: bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Resolve ``value_num``/``value_text`` into a unified ``value`` column and, if ``wide``, pivot to
      one column per variable via :meth:`_to_wide`; otherwise return the long frame with a fresh index.



   .. py:method:: _coerce_wide_measurement_dtypes(df: pandas.DataFrame, *, table_name: str) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Restore numeric dtypes on wide-pivoted measurement columns.

      ``_resolve_measurement_values`` builds a single ``value`` series from ``value_num`` with a
      ``value_text`` fallback, which upcasts the whole series to ``object`` whenever *any* text
      variable is in the query. The subsequent pivot then leaves numeric variables (e.g.
      ``hematocrit``) as object-dtype floats, and Patsy treats them as categoricals
      (``Hematocrit[T.36.0]``, …). Coerce columns whose catalog ``value_kind`` is numeric back to
      float64.



   .. py:method:: _resolve_measurement_values(df: pandas.DataFrame) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Add a unified ``value`` column, preferring ``value_num`` and falling back to ``value_text``
      row-wise where the numeric value is missing.



   .. py:method:: _to_wide(df: pandas.DataFrame, definition: nvitk.db.catalog.TableDefinition, *, image_wide_single_variable: bool | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Pivot a long measurement frame to wide form: one row per entity (``wide_index_columns``) and
      one column per composed key (region/variable/frame, see :func:`_compose_image_wide_keys` for
      ``image_measurements`` or :meth:`_compose_wide_keys` otherwise), values from the ``value`` column.



   .. py:method:: _compose_wide_keys(df: pandas.DataFrame, key_columns: list[str]) -> pandas.Series

      Join *key_columns* per row with ``__`` (skipping empty parts) to form wide-pivot column keys.



   .. py:method:: _relative_path(path: pathlib.Path) -> str

      *path* expressed relative to the dataset root, as a POSIX-style string for catalog storage.



.. py:function:: get_repo_from_settings(return_xnat_config: bool = False) -> DataRepo | nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig

   Get :class:`DataRepo` from settings file, optionally with :class:`XnatConnectionConfig`.


.. py:class:: SQLiteIndex(db_path: str | pathlib.Path)

   Path to ``catalog.sqlite`` (or configured index); :meth:`build` refreshes from Parquet.


   .. py:attribute:: db_path


   .. py:method:: exists() -> bool

      True if the SQLite database file has been built.



   .. py:method:: build(catalog: nvitk.db.catalog.DatasetCatalog, *, tables: list[str] | None = None) -> pathlib.Path

      Rebuild the SQLite database from *catalog*'s Parquet tables (all tables, or just *tables*):
      replaces each table wholesale, indexes its key/index columns, and records
      ``schema_version``/``dataset_name`` in a ``_dataset_meta`` table. Tables whose Parquet file
      doesn't exist yet are skipped.



   .. py:method:: query_table(table_name: str, *, columns: list[str] | None = None, filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

      Run a filtered ``SELECT`` against *table_name* in the SQLite index, projecting *columns*
      (all if unset) and translating *filters* via :func:`~nvitk.db.filters.build_sql_where`.



.. py:function:: register_dicom_tree(dicom_root: str | pathlib.Path, *, source: str = 'local_dicom', pipeline_id: str | None = None, pipeline_name: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Build ``assets`` rows for DICOM trees under ``dicom_root`` (one row per file).


.. py:function:: upsert_dicom_assets(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, dicom_root: str | pathlib.Path, *, source: str = 'local_dicom', pipeline_id: str | None = None, pipeline_name: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None, dry_run: bool = False, build_sqlite_index: bool = False) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Compute DICOM asset rows and upsert into ``repo`` unless ``dry_run``.


.. py:function:: register_nifti_tree(nifti_root: str | pathlib.Path, *, source: str = 'local_nifti', pipeline_id: str | None = None, pipeline_name: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Build ``assets`` rows for TOF and 4DFlow NIfTI trees under ``nifti_root``.


.. py:function:: upsert_nifti_assets(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, nifti_root: str | pathlib.Path, *, source: str = 'local_nifti', pipeline_id: str | None = None, pipeline_name: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None, dry_run: bool = False, build_sqlite_index: bool = False) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Compute asset rows and upsert into ``repo`` unless ``dry_run``.

   Build local pipeline-bundle asset rows via :func:`register_local_pipeline_tree` and upsert them
   into the ``assets`` table (unless ``dry_run`` or the frame is empty).


.. py:function:: classify_scan(series_description: str | None, quality: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None

   Classify a scan by its *series_description* (and optional QC *quality*) into a
   ``{modality, orientation, sequence, ...}`` dict, matching BrainVIEW/VWI_BB, TOF/MRA, 4D-flow, resting-
   state fMRI, carotid QF, QSM/SWI, and other known sequence patterns in priority order. Returns
   ``None`` when the description matches nothing, or when *quality* is present and not ``"usable"``
   (except for the BrainVIEW/VWI_BB case, which is quality-independent).


.. py:function:: connect_xnat(config: nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig)

   Open an ``xnat`` session for *config*, resolving credentials via :func:`_resolve_xnat_login`.
   Raises ``BackendUnavailableError`` if the ``xnat`` package isn't installed, or an XNAT auth error
   (with a help message) if no usable credentials were found.


.. py:function:: list_scans_for_subject(repo: Any, project_id: str, subject_uid: str) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Scans for *subject_uid* in *project_id* (joined with sessions).


.. py:function:: list_subjects_for_project(repo: Any, project_id: str) -> list[str]

   Distinct ``subject_uid`` values with sessions in *project_id*.


.. py:function:: resolve_xnat_scan_from_scan_row(session: Any, row: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any

   Return the XNAT *scan* handle for a ``scans`` table row (uses ``session_uid`` and ``scan_id``).


.. py:function:: sync_xnat_project(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, config: nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig, *, catalog_path: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, subjects: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, subjects_file: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, id_type: str = 'subject', requested_sequences: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, download_root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, download_dicoms: bool = False, download_niftis: bool = False, nifti_resource_label: str = 'NIFTI', nifti_download_root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, skip_existing: bool = True, build_sqlite_index: bool = False, cohort_id: str | None = None, source_batch_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, pandas.DataFrame]

   Sync an XNAT project's subjects, sessions, scans, and (optionally) DICOM/NIfTI downloads into the
   dataset catalog tables. Resolves which subjects/sequences to pull via *catalog_path*/*subjects*/
   *subjects_file* and *requested_sequences* (falling back to the project's default sequence list),
   classifies each scan with :mod:`nvitk.db.xnat_projects` helpers, writes ``subjects``/``sessions``/
   ``scans``/``assets``/``subject_ids`` rows, enrolls synced subjects into *cohort_id*, and optionally
   downloads DICOM/NIfTI resources and rebuilds the SQLite index. Returns the written catalog frames.


.. py:function:: xnat_sequence_to_asset_slot(sequence_label: str) -> str

   Map XNAT sequence labels (see :func:`classify_scan`) to canonical ``asset_slot`` names.


.. py:function:: download_experiment_resource(experiment: Any, resource_label: str, dest_dir: pathlib.Path, *, overwrite: bool = False) -> pathlib.Path

   Download an experiment-level XNAT resource into *dest_dir*.

   After download, unwraps xnatpy's ``{experiment}/resources/{label}/files`` nesting
   so *dest_dir* matches the local pipeline results layout.


.. py:function:: inspect_xnat_pipeline_resource(experiment: Any, resource_label: str) -> dict[str, Any]

   Return availability metadata for one experiment resource (no download).


.. py:function:: list_pipeline_assets_for_subject(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, project_id: str, subject_uid: str) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Return indexed pipeline bundle rows for *subject_uid*.

   Includes ``eicab`` / ``qvtpy`` / ``4dflows`` experiment resources. Derived
   ``4dflows`` file rows (``source=xnat_4dflows``) are collapsed to a single
   downloadable ``pipeline_4dflows`` bundle entry when no bundle row exists.


.. py:function:: sync_xnat_pipeline_resources(repo: nvitk.db.repo.DataRepo, config: nvitk.db.xnat_config.XnatConnectionConfig, *, catalog_path: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, subjects: str | Iterable[str] | None = None, subjects_file: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, id_type: str = 'subject', resources: Iterable[str] = QVTPY_PIPELINE_RESOURCES, download_root: str | pathlib.Path | None = None, download_resources: bool = False, overwrite_downloads: bool = False, skip_existing_downloads: bool = True, build_sqlite_index: bool = False, source_batch_id: str | None = None) -> pandas.DataFrame

   Index qvtpy/eICAB experiment resources on XNAT into ``assets``.


.. py:function:: classify_experiment_ia_pet_v5(scans: list[Any], *, experiment_label: str | None = None) -> list[tuple[Any, str, str, str, dict[str, Any]]]

   Classify all scans in one IA_PET_V5 experiment.

   Returns ``(scan, scan_id, series_description, quality, classification)`` tuples
   with one entry per sequence label (first scan wins for duplicates).


.. py:function:: classify_scan_for_project(project_id: str, series_description: str | None, quality: str | None = None, *, scan_id: str | None = None, experiment_label: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None

   Dispatch scan classification for a registered XNAT project.


.. py:function:: classify_scan_ia_pet_v5(series_description: str | None, quality: str | None = None, *, scan_id: str | None = None, experiment_label: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None

   Classify a single PESA-Fat IA_PET_V5 scan (Dixon MR + CT/PET).

   Dixon scans return a candidate marker (``dixon=True``); region assignment
   requires :func:`classify_experiment_ia_pet_v5` at experiment scope.


.. py:function:: get_xnat_project(project_id: str) -> XnatProjectSpec

   Return the registered :class:`XnatProjectSpec` for *project_id*; raises ``KeyError`` (listing
   known ids) if unregistered.


.. py:function:: list_xnat_project_ids() -> list[str]

   Sorted ids of every registered :data:`XNAT_PROJECTS` entry.


.. py:class:: XnatConnectionConfig

   Resolved XNAT connection settings (server, project, credentials, TLS/timeout options) ready to
   pass to :func:`~nvitk.db.xnat.connect_xnat`. Build via :func:`resolve_xnat_connection` rather than
   constructing directly.


   .. py:attribute:: server
      :type:  str


   .. py:attribute:: project
      :type:  str


   .. py:attribute:: user
      :type:  str | None
      :value: None



   .. py:attribute:: password
      :type:  str | None
      :value: None



   .. py:attribute:: netrc_file
      :type:  str | None
      :value: None



   .. py:attribute:: verify
      :type:  bool
      :value: False



   .. py:attribute:: default_timeout
      :type:  int
      :value: 600



   .. py:method:: __post_init__() -> None

      Normalize ``server``/``project`` to non-empty strings via :func:`_coerce_xnat_identifier`.



.. py:function:: load_xnat_profile(path: pathlib.Path | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]

   Load ``xnat`` profile dict from JSON or YAML.

   If ``path`` is ``None``, uses ``NVITK_XNAT_CONFIG`` if set, else the first
   existing file among ``~/.config/nvitk/xnat.{yaml,yml,json}``.

   YAML requires PyYAML (``pip install pyyaml`` or ``nvitk[xnat]``).


.. py:function:: resolve_xnat_connection(profile: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, *, server: str | None = None, project: str | None = None, user: str | None = None, password: str | None = None, netrc_file: str | None = None, verify: bool | None = None, default_timeout: int | None = None) -> XnatConnectionConfig

   Build :class:`XnatConnectionConfig` from profile, environment, and overrides.

   Password resolution when not explicitly provided:

   1. ``profile['password']`` (discouraged for shared files)
   2. ``password_env`` env var name in profile → ``os.environ``
   3. ``password_keyring: true`` in profile → keyring for ``xnat:{server}``
   4. ``XNAT_PASSWORD`` environment variable
